task.description: WF-02 Step 2c mandatory security review for REQ-034 (registration into 'requested' for an approval-gated event). Verify S4, S7, S8 hold; double-request refusal scopes to the requesting user's own row only; no new PII category is introduced.
acceptance_criteria: S4: qrToken stays NULL for a 'requested' outcome, traced via registerForEvent's write path, not the summary
S7: the 'requested' path adds zero capacity check, and a 'requested' row is excluded from every seats_taken/capacity computation anywhere in the codebase, not just at write time
S8: exactly one AuditLog row per requested outcome, correct actor/action/entity/entity_id, in the same atomic transaction as the registration write
double-request 'already-registered' refusal shows only the requesting user's own row, no cross-user leak
no new consent/PII category introduced (S1 N/A check)

result.summary:
Re-derived each invariant directly against the diff (git diff master...HEAD), not from BACKEND-DEV's or REVIEWER's summaries.

S4 (single-purpose token): traced apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's registerForEvent step 8 directly. `const qrToken = outcome.kind === "admitted" ? generateQrToken() : null;` (line 196) is byte-for-byte unchanged by this diff -- confirmed via the diff hunk, which shows zero edits to this line. Since decideRegistrationOutcome's requiresApproval branch (row 6 of the first-match-wins table, line 75-76) now returns { kind: "requested" } and this branch sits before the { kind: "admitted" } branch (row 7, line 78-79) in the same if-chain, a 'requested' outcome can never equal 'admitted' at the ternary -- qrToken is structurally null for every 'requested' write, the same way it already is for 'waitlisted'. The INSERT/UPDATE writes `qrToken` (the null value) into registrations.qr_token directly (lines 210/223) inside the same transaction as the admission write -- there is no window where a row exists with a non-null token before this outcome kind existed. Constructed the negative case myself: if 'requested' were accidentally added to the qrToken ternary's true-branch, the existing test registration.db.test.ts's new assertion `expect(outcome.qrToken).toBeUndefined()` (added in this diff) would fail, and RegisterForEventResult's spread (`...(qrToken !== null ? { qrToken } : {})`, line 258) would also start returning a token to the caller -- neither happens; ran `npx vitest run apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts -t requires_approval` myself (see git_evidence) and it passes with qrToken undefined. AC5/S4 hold.

S7 (capacity -- seats_taken = count(admission='admitted') only): traced §0.2's claim directly rather than trusting it. decideRegistrationOutcome's requiresApproval branch (row 6, line 75) sits strictly before the `if (input.seatsLeft > 0)` comparison (row 7, line 78) in the same function body, and returns immediately -- seatsLeft's computed value is read into the input struct (registerForEvent line 172, unconditionally, as it always was) but is never inspected on the 'requested' path; this is structural, not incidental (the return statement makes row 7 unreachable for requiresApproval=true, regardless of what seatsLeft numerically is -- confirmed for the AC4 over-capacity case by reading the branch: nothing between row 6's return and row 7 could ever execute for this input). This satisfies AC4/S7's write-side half exactly as designed -- no capacity check exists on this path to bypass.

For the downstream half (a requested row must never be counted as occupying a seat ANYWHERE, not just at write time) I did my own repo-wide grep for every seat/capacity-counting call site rather than accepting the design doc's claim. Grepped for countAdmitted|seatsLeft|computeSeatsLeft|admission ===|seats_taken across apps/bot/src. There is exactly ONE function in the entire codebase that counts admitted registrations for capacity purposes: `countAdmittedRegistrations` (apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts lines 467-476) -- its WHERE clause is `and(eq(registrations.eventId, eventId), eq(registrations.admission, "admitted"))`, a strict equality filter, not a NOT IN/exclusion list -- so 'requested' (or any other non-'admitted' state) is excluded by construction, not by an enumerated exclusion that could miss a state. Every capacity-relevant call site in the codebase calls this same function: registerForEvent itself (registration.ts:165-169, inlined identically), promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible (registration.ts:393-396, inlined identically), handlers/checkin.ts:289, handlers/event.ts:186/337/505, handlers/start.ts:165, domain/walkin.ts:277. No second/duplicate seat-counting query exists anywhere -- confirmed by the grep returning only this one WHERE-admission='admitted' shape across the whole apps/bot/src tree. A 'requested' row is therefore excluded from seats_taken at every downstream computation, not merely at the write path. S7 holds both at write time and at every read/display site.

S8 (audit logging): traced registerForEvent's transaction body directly (registration.ts lines 123-260, one `db.transaction(async (tx) => {...})` wrapping the entire function). The row lock (step 2), the outcome decision, the INSERT/UPDATE (step 8), and the `writeAuditLog(tx, {...})` call (lines 241-253) all execute against the SAME `tx` handle inside the SAME transaction callback -- there is no early return, no separate connection, and no code path between the INSERT/UPDATE and the writeAuditLog call that could commit one without the other (both are awaited sequentially inside one callback whose promise resolution is what triggers the transaction commit). The audit action for a 'requested' outcome resolves via the three-way ternary (lines 243-248) to the literal string "registration.request" -- confirmed this string is otherwise unused anywhere else in the codebase (grep found it only in this diff's own registration.ts, registration.db.test.ts, and handlers/registration.test.ts/my.test.ts as an expected value, no collision with any other write path's action string). actorUserId is the requesting user's own userId (the function's own `userId` parameter, matching admit/waitlist's identical `actorUserId: userId` -- the actor IS the person requesting, correctly), entity is the fixed literal "registration", entityId is `insertedRow.id` (the just-created/reused row's own id, returned from the same INSERT/UPDATE via `.returning({ id: registrations.id })`), payload is `{ eventId }`. This is exactly one writeAuditLog call on this code path, unconditionally reached whenever the writing-outcome branch is taken (the guard at line 189 already returns early for every non-writing kind before this call is ever reached, so no double-count and no zero-count case exists for a genuine 'requested' write). AC6/S8 hold.

Double-request scoping: decideRegistrationOutcome's row 1 (`existingAdmission !== null` -> `{ kind: "already-registered", admission: existingAdmission }`, line 60-61) is fed `existingAdmission`, which registerForEvent computes (lines 147-158) from a SELECT scoped by `and(eq(registrations.eventId, eventId), eq(registrations.userId, userId))` -- `userId` here is the CALLING user's own id (the function's own parameter, sourced from the handler's authenticated ctx, not any caller-suppliable id), so the row read back and echoed in the refusal is structurally always the requesting user's own row -- there is no code path by which another user's admission value could reach this branch. composeRegistrationReply's 'already-registered' branch (handlers/registration.ts, unchanged by this diff) renders only `STATUS_CATALOG_KEY[outcome.admission]`, a fixed enum-to-string map -- it carries no other user's identifying data (no name, no other row's id) at all, for any admission value including 'requested'. Constructed the negative case: even if two different users both had 'requested' registrations for the same event, each user's own registerForEvent call independently re-runs this same userId-scoped SELECT, so user A's reply can never be built from user B's row -- there is no shared/global lookup here. AC3 and S2/S3's cross-user-leak concern both hold.

S1 (no new PII/consent category): this requirement adds no new column, no new table, and no new field to any existing consent-bearing entity (User, Profile) -- confirmed by `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/db` returning empty (no schema.ts changes in this diff at all, consistent with the design's own 'no schema change' claim, independently re-verified rather than trusted). The only new data captured is the outcome kind string itself ('requested') and the audit action string -- neither is a new PII category, both reuse the existing registration/consent flow from REQ-011/REQ-020. S1 is N/A -- no new consent surface is created, and the existing three-consent model (store/broadcast/publish) is untouched by this diff.

No other S-item applies: no qr_token/InviteCode generation change (S4's generation half untouched -- generateQrToken itself has zero diff lines), no EventStaff/role check surface touched (this is a member-facing registration path, not a check-in/authorization path -- S2/S5/S6/S12 N/A), no export/CSV path touched (S12 N/A), no broadcast/notification kind added (S9/S10 N/A, and §0.4 of the design correctly traces why this stays a direct reply rather than a ledgered send -- independently confirmed by reading notification.ts's NotificationKind union, which is untouched by this diff), no plaintext PII logging introduced (S11 N/A -- the new i18n strings and audit payload carry only eventId, no phone/email), no deletion/anonymization path touched (S13 N/A), no speaker/publish-consent surface touched (S14 N/A).

Migrations: no migration file appears in this diff at all (confirmed via `git diff master...HEAD --stat`, no drizzle migration files listed) -- the 0005-orm-drizzle.md sign-off duty does not apply to this run.
